Definition: Opening dishes intended to be shared or eaten before the main course.
Inclusion rules: Items served at the beginning of a meal; small cold or hot plates eaten communally.
Exclusion rules: Main courses; desserts; sides offered only as accompaniments to another item.
Alternative names and synonyms: Openers; Appetizers; Antipasti; Petiscos; Hors d'oeuvres; Mezze (partial); Small plates; Sharing plates; Amuse-bouche
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Mezze usage predominates in North Africa and the Middle East.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Liquid or semi-liquid dishes served as a course or as a light meal.
Inclusion rules: Items whose primary serving form is broth-based; thickened soups; chilled soups; traditional broths.
Exclusion rules: Stews served over a staple with no liquid presentation; beverages; dressings.
Alternative names and synonyms: Soup; Consomme; Broth; Bisque; Chowder; Stew soup; Potaje
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Uji and other thickened African porridges sit at the boundary with FAM-05.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Raw or lightly dressed vegetable and leaf dishes.
Inclusion rules: Leaf, mixed and composed vegetable salads served as a course or light meal.
Exclusion rules: Cooked vegetable sides; raw relishes that function as mandatory accompaniments (see FAM-04).
Alternative names and synonyms: Salad; Salade; Ensalada; Green salad; Mixed salad; Chef salad
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Acar and kachumbari belong to FAM-04, not here, despite similar ingredients.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Small raw or preserved items served alongside a main item rather than as a dish in their own right.
Inclusion rules: Raw tomato-onion relishes; pickled vegetables; chutneys; sauces-on-the-side sold as separate lines.
Exclusion rules: Cooked sauces served as modifiers; salads composed as a course; side vegetables sold as portions.
Alternative names and synonyms: Relish; Kachumbari; Kachumber; Acar; Atchara; Chutney; Sambal; Slaw; Shatini; Chakalaka; Pickle
Regional or cuisine relevance: Strong in East Africa (kachumbari, acar) and South Africa (shatini, chakalaka); also South Asian cuisine.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Starchy base components that accompany or compose a meal, and are frequently sold as separate priced lines.
Inclusion rules: Maize, cassava, rice, plantain, bread and dumpling bases eaten with stews, sauces or proteins.
Exclusion rules: Dishes where the staple is the dish's identity in Western cuisine (pizza bases, burger buns); see FAM-16.
Alternative names and synonyms: Staple; Base; Swallow; Ugali; Posho; Fufu; Pap; Sadza; Wali; Akume; Chapati; Injera; Kisra
Regional or cuisine relevance: Core to East, West and Southern African cuisine. Structural base of the EAC meal model.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Slow-cooked, liquid or semi-liquid dishes served with a staple.
Inclusion rules: Beef, chicken, vegetable, groundnut, bean and coconut-milk stews; khatta and curry preparations.
Exclusion rules: Grilled or roasted meat; soups served in a bowl; sauces offered only as modifiers.
Alternative names and synonyms: Stew; Curry; Sauce-based dish; Potjie; Stew (sauce for ugali)
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Groundnut sauce (Uganda), makange (Tanzania) and mchuzi are regional instances.

Definition: Legume dishes in which the pulse is the principal component rather than a garnish.
Inclusion rules: Cooked bean dishes; groundnut sauces; lentil and chickpea dishes; bean and maize combinations.
Exclusion rules: Bean salads served cold; pulse-based snacks.
Alternative names and synonyms: Beans; Ibiharage; Ibitoke/Igitoke; Imbize; Groundnut sauce; Stewed beans; Palava
Regional or cuisine relevance: Regional in East Africa, where pulses are a staple base rather than a side. Strong in Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, Kenya.

Definition: Items cooked over direct radiant or convective heat and served as a main.
Inclusion rules: Steaks, chops, fillets, whole joints and mixed grills cooked to order.
Exclusion rules: Skewered small meat portions (see FAM-09); roasts cooked in an oven.
Alternative names and synonyms: Grill; From the Grill; Barbecue; Braai; BBQ; Charcoal grilled; Smoked; Rotisserie
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Braai is the Southern African form; mishkaki in East Africa.

Definition: Meat, poultry or fish cut into small portions and cooked on skewers.
Inclusion rules: Beef, goat, chicken, fish and offal skewers; rolled and wrapped skewer dishes.
Exclusion rules: Whole grilled joints; skewered vegetables served as a side.
Alternative names and synonyms: Brochettes; Brochette; Mishkaki; Mshikaki; Skewers; Kebab; Satay; Brochettes mixtes
Regional or cuisine relevance: Central to Burundian, Rwandan and Ugandan menus. Mishkaki is the East African form.

Definition: Non-grilled principal meat and poultry dishes.
Inclusion rules: Stews, roasts, pan-fried and casseroled meat dishes; poultry dishes.
Exclusion rules: Grilled items in FAM-08; skewered items in FAM-09.
Alternative names and synonyms: Meat; Nyama; Poultry; Inyama; Goat; Mbuzi; Beef; Chicken; Impala; Ostrich
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Game meats (impala, ostrich, antelope) are prominent in Southern and East African menus.

Definition: Fish, shellfish and other marine items as principal components.
Inclusion rules: Grilled, fried and stewed fish; freshwater lake fish; shellfish; whole fish served with staple.
Exclusion rules: Dried or smoked fish sold as an accompaniment; fish-based sauces.
Alternative names and synonyms: Fish; Seafood; Samaki; Tilapia; Mbadi; Pike; Ndagala; Crustaceans; Shellfish
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Lake Tanganyika and Victoria freshwater fish are prominent in Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania and Kenya.

Definition: Principal dishes formulated without meat or without animal products.
Inclusion rules: Vegetable curries, stews, grains and vegetable mains; dairy- and egg-free preparations.
Exclusion rules: Vegetarian items that are sides, salads or starters; dietary suitability tags applied to non-vegetarian items.
Alternative names and synonyms: Vegetable mains; Vegan mains; Meat-free; Vegetarian entrees; Sides (vegetarian only)
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Category usage is uneven; in East Africa vegetable dishes are more often stews in FAM-06 or FAM-07.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Dishes in which rice is the principal component rather than an accompaniment.
Inclusion rules: Biryani, pilau, jollof, fried rice, arroz, rice and bean plates.
Exclusion rules: Plain rice sold as a side or staple line (see FAM-05).
Alternative names and synonyms: Rice; Biryani; Biriani; Pilau; Pulao; Jollof; Fried rice; Rice bowl
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Biryani and pilau are prominent in East African menus; jollof in West Africa.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Dishes in which pasta is the principal component.
Inclusion rules: Spaghetti, penne, lasagne, risotto, filled pasta, pasta specials.
Exclusion rules: Plain pasta sold as a staple line; house-branded headings that are not culinary types.
Alternative names and synonyms: Pasta; Pasta dishes; Italian; Noodles (Italian); Risotto; Lasagne; Spaghetti
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. 'Pasta Club' as a house-branded heading is observed in East African hotel menus.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Dishes in which a wheat or rice noodle is the principal component.
Inclusion rules: Stir-fried, soup and noodle-bowl preparations; regional noodle styles.
Exclusion rules: Pasta in the Italian sense; plain noodles sold as a staple line.
Alternative names and synonyms: Noodles; Noodle bowl; Chow mein; Lo mein; Udon; Ramen; Noodle soup
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Asian noodle dishes are common in East African hotel and lounge menus.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Flat, leavened or unleavened breads baked or griddled as a principal item.
Inclusion rules: Wood-fired and pan pizzas; flatbread bases; naan, chapati and wraps served filled (see FAM-19).
Exclusion rules: Bread sold as a bakery staple (see FAM-17); filled wraps classified under FAM-19.
Alternative names and synonyms: Pizza; Pizzas; Flatbreads; Naan; Chapati; Paratha; Injera
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Ugandan chapati is a cultural form distinct from South Asian chapati in naming only.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Leavened and unleavened breads sold as individual items.
Inclusion rules: Sourdough, rye, baguette, rolls, flatbreads sold unbought, stuffed breads.
Exclusion rules: Pastries and confectionery (FAM-29); breads used only as a sandwich base.
Alternative names and synonyms: Bread; Breads; Bakery; Loaves; Rolls; Baguette; Sourdough; Chapatti; Mandazi; Mahambri
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Mandazi, mahambri and vitumbua are East African fried or sweet breads.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Filled bread or wrap sandwiches served as a principal item.
Inclusion rules: Filled rolls, ciabatta, baguette, chapati wraps, rolex, egg-and-chapati rolls.
Exclusion rules: Burgers as a distinct format (FAM-19); plain bread.
Alternative names and synonyms: Sandwiches; Wraps; Rolls; Sub; Panini; Club sandwich; Rollex; Chapati roll
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Rolex is an East African form combining omelette, sausage and cabbage in chapati.

Definition: Sandwich format with a patty or formed protein filling.
Inclusion rules: Beef, chicken, fish, veggie and house burgers with named patties.
Exclusion rules: Filled sandwiches without a formed patty (FAM-18).
Alternative names and synonyms: Burgers; Burger; Cheeseburger; Veggie burger; House burger
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Widely observed as a distinct format across full-service and delivery menus.

Definition: Dishes whose principal component is egg.
Inclusion rules: Omelettes, egg rolls, frittatas, egg curries, boiled and fried egg plates.
Exclusion rules: Eggs as a breakfast component within a breakfast set (FAM-21).
Alternative names and synonyms: Eggs; Omelette; Omelet; Egg dishes; Frittata; Scrambled eggs
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Egg-and-chapati rolls are a Kampala street-food form observed on live menus.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Items constituting a breakfast meal, served during the breakfast service period.
Inclusion rules: Egg plates, full English and continental plates, porridge, pancakes, waffles, breakfast platters.
Exclusion rules: Items merely available at breakfast (FAM-20, FAM-17, FAM-31).
Alternative names and synonyms: Breakfast; Morning; Morning Bakery; Hot Breakfast; Continental; Full English
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Buffet-zone naming varies; see DKS 2455-style core menus.

Definition: Items constituting a mid-morning meal combining breakfast and lunch characteristics.
Inclusion rules: Brunch plates, brunch platters, eggs benedict, brunch set compositions.
Exclusion rules: Standard breakfast items (FAM-21) unless the business treats brunch as a distinct offering.
Alternative names and synonyms: Brunch; Weekend brunch; Brunch set; Sunday brunch
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Widely used in East African hospitality and cafe menus.

Definition: Small items bought as between-meal food or as casual street fare.
Inclusion rules: Samosa, spring roll, samosas, puff-puff, chops, fried dough, roasted maize, chips.
Exclusion rules: Starters served table-service (FAM-01); sides (FAM-04).
Alternative names and synonyms: Snacks; Street food; Small chops; Chops; Snacks & Starters; Bites; Nibbles
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Small chops is a West African category; samosas and chips are ubiquitous in East Africa.

Definition: Large-format items intended for table sharing.
Inclusion rules: Mixed grills, sharing boards, platters for two or more, party platters.
Exclusion rules: Individual portion items; meal deals (which are items, not categories).
Alternative names and synonyms: Platters; Platers to Share; To Share; Sharing; Boards; Feast; Mixed Grill Platter
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. 'Platers to Share' (misspelt) is observed on a live Kampala menu.

Definition: Portions prepared for children, typically reduced size.
Inclusion rules: Junior mains, kids plates, children's roast dinners.
Exclusion rules: Any reduced-portion adult dish without a declared children's intent.
Alternative names and synonyms: Kids; Children's; Junior; Little; Petit; Bambino
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Rarely observed in East African menus during this study.

Definition: Sweet dishes served at the end of a meal.
Inclusion rules: Cakes, pastries, puddings, ice-cream-based desserts, fruit desserts.
Exclusion rules: Sweet breads and confectionery (FAM-29); celebration cakes (FAM-27).
Alternative names and synonyms: Desserts; Dessert; Dolci; Sweet; Afters; Pudding; Sweetmeats
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Heading choice varies: Desserts, Sweets, Dolci and Afters all in observed use.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Whole or portioned cakes designed for gifting and celebration.
Inclusion rules: Birthday cakes, wedding cakes, whole-sheet cakes sold by size or weight.
Exclusion rules: Individual cake slices served as desserts (FAM-26).
Alternative names and synonyms: Cakes; Cake; Celebration cake; Wedding cake; Custom cake; Tiered cake
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Served whole or by weight, so size handling is required.
Applicable business types: Bakery; Cafe; Chain; Independent restaurant; Independent restaurant

Definition: Frozen sweet items.
Inclusion rules: Ice cream, sorbet, frozen yoghurt, ice-cream cakes.
Exclusion rules: Chilled but unfrozen puddings.
Alternative names and synonyms: Ice cream; Frozen; Gelato; Sorbet; Ice
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global.
Applicable business types: Bakery; Cafe; Chain; Independent restaurant; Independent restaurant

Definition: Baked sweet items and small confectionery produced by a bakery.
Inclusion rules: Croissants, pains, tarts, pastries, biscuits, chocolates, sweets.
Exclusion rules: Cakes (FAM-27); sweet breads (FAM-17).
Alternative names and synonyms: Pastries; Pastry; Bakes; Sweets; Confectionery; Cookies; Biscuits; Cakes and Sweets
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. ArtCaffe combines this with breads, cakes, drinks and breakfast in one category set.

Definition: Small cold dishes served communally at the start of a meal.
Inclusion rules: Hummus, moutabal, baba ganoush, fattoush, labneh, olives, flatbread accompaniments.
Exclusion rules: Hot starters (FAM-01); salads composed as a course (FAM-03).
Alternative names and synonyms: Mezze; Mezza; Cold appetizers; Cold starters; Antipasti; Mezedesh
Regional or cuisine relevance: Strong in North Africa and the Middle East; also observed in West African small-chop formats.

Definition: Hot beverages based on coffee, tea or infusion.
Inclusion rules: Espresso drinks, filter coffee, brewed tea, infusions, chocolate drinks, spiced tea.
Exclusion rules: Iced coffee and cold brews (FAM-32); cocoa-based dessert drinks (FAM-26).
Alternative names and synonyms: Coffee; Espresso; Hot Coffees; Tea; Teas; Brew Bar; Infusions; Cappuccino; Latte
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Spiced, sweetened and ginger tea forms are prominent in East Africa and belong here, not in a tea house family.

Definition: Chilled non-alcoholic beverages, including chilled coffee.
Inclusion rules: Iced coffee, cold brew, iced tea, malt and flavoured milks, bottled soft drinks.
Exclusion rules: Hot beverages (FAM-31); juices (FAM-33); water (FAM-34).
Alternative names and synonyms: Cold drinks; Iced; Iced Coffee; Cold Brew; Chilled; Milkshakes (non-fruit)
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. ArtCaffe publishes a combined Hot & Iced Coffees category; a split is permitted.

Definition: Fruit-based and blended non-alcoholic beverages.
Inclusion rules: Fresh juices, fruit salads blended, protein shakes, smoothie bowls, malt drinks served as beverages.
Exclusion rules: Whole fruit; vegetable juices sold as a health preparation.
Alternative names and synonyms: Juices; Juice; Smoothies; Shakes; Fresh Juices; Milkshakes; Boosters
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Fresh juice lines are widely listed in West African menus; smoothies appear in East African cafes.
Applicable business types: Cafe; Bakery; Chain; Hotel; Delivery-only kitchen

Definition: Still and sparkling water, soft drinks, soda and mixers.
Inclusion rules: Mineral water, flavoured water, sodas, tonic, mixers, kombucha.
Exclusion rules: Beer and malt (FAM-35); juices (FAM-33).
Alternative names and synonyms: Water; Soft Drinks; Sodas; Mixers; Drinks; Beverages; Refreshments
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Frequently bundled with food under a single 'Drinks' heading, which PEWA should discourage.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Beer and beer-adjacent malt beverages.
Inclusion rules: Draught and draught-cask beer; bottled and canned lager, ale, stout and malt; non-alcoholic beer.
Exclusion rules: Wine and cider (FAM-36); traditional fermented drinks (FAM-39).
Alternative names and synonyms: Beer; Beers; Lager; Ales; Stout; Draught; Draft; Bottled; Cans; Malt; Non-alcoholic beer
Regional or cuisine relevance: Strong in East Africa: lager, malt and non-alcoholic axes are all material; see brand portfolio structure.
Applicable business types: Bar; Hotel; Cafe; Hotel; Delivery-only kitchen

Definition: Grape, cider and fortified wines.
Inclusion rules: Red, white, rose, sparkling by the glass and bottle; dessert wine; cider.
Exclusion rules: Beer (FAM-35); spirits (FAM-37).
Alternative names and synonyms: Wine; Wines; By the Glass; Cellar; Red; White; Rose; Cider; Champagne; Port; Sherry
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. By-the-glass versus by-bottle is the standard split observed across bar menus.

Definition: Distilled alcoholic beverages sold by the serve or neat.
Inclusion rules: Whisky, vodka, gin, rum, tequila, mezcal, brandy, liqueurs, aquavit, by the pour.
Exclusion rules: Cocktails (FAM-38); beer (FAM-35).
Alternative names and synonyms: Spirits; Spirits list; By the Pour; Neat; Pours; Back bar; Liqueurs; Aperitifs
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Grouped by base spirit in observed practice.

Definition: Mixed alcoholic drinks and their alcohol-free counterparts.
Inclusion rules: Signature and house cocktails, classics, seasonal cocktails, mocktails, virgin cocktails, zero-proof serves.
Exclusion rules: Neat spirit pours (FAM-37); soft drinks (FAM-34).
Alternative names and synonyms: Cocktails; Signature cocktails; Classics; House Cocktails; Mocktails; No & Low; Zero proof; Virgin cocktails
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Low and no-alcohol treated as a first-class section in current bar practice.

Definition: Indigenous and fermented beverages prepared on premises or sold as regional specialties.
Inclusion rules: Banana beer, sorghum beer, chibuku, palm wine, honey wine, spiced traditional tea, fermented milk drinks.
Exclusion rules: Commercial packaged lager (FAM-35); standard tea infusions (FAM-31).
Alternative names and synonyms: Pombe; Urwagwa; Urwarwa; Chibuku; Uji; Traditional drinks; Local beer; Honey wine; Ata
Regional or cuisine relevance: Regional. Central to Burundian and Rwandan beverage offerings; also present in Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.

Definition: Smoking-related products offered at food and beverage venues.
Inclusion rules: Waterpipe, shisha flavours, cigarettes, cigars.
Exclusion rules: All non-smoking beverages and foods.
Alternative names and synonyms: Shisha; Waterpipe; Hookah; Tobacco; Smokes
Regional or cuisine relevance: Regional. Common in hospitality venues across East Africa and the Middle East.

Definition: Maize, cassava, sorghum and millet-based bases served with stews and sauces.
Inclusion rules: Posho, ugali, ubugali, ubugari, bugali, pap, sadza, akume, kimea, walla.
Exclusion rules: Rice dishes (FAM-13); bread sold as a bakery line (FAM-17).
Alternative names and synonyms: Posho; Ugali; Ubugali; Ubugari; Bugali; Pap; Sadza; Akume; Walla; Kimea; Fufu (East African use)
Regional or cuisine relevance: Burundi, Rwanda, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania.

Definition: Sauce-led dishes served over a staple, including groundnut and coconut-milk preparations.
Inclusion rules: Groundnut sauce, peanut stew, beef stew with sauce, makange, mchuzi, curry with rice, beans with sauce.
Exclusion rules: Soups served in a bowl (FAM-02); grills (FAM-08).
Alternative names and synonyms: Stew; Groundnut sauce; Peanut stew; Makange; Mchuzi; Sauce (served with ugali)
Regional or cuisine relevance: Uganda, Tanzania, Kenya, Rwanda.

Definition: Skewered and rolled small meat and fish portions.
Inclusion rules: Beef brochettes, goat brochettes, chicken brochettes, fish brochettes, sauced brochette variants.
Exclusion rules: Grilled steaks and chops (FAM-08).
Alternative names and synonyms: Brochettes; Brochette; Mishkaki; Mshikaki; Brochettes mixtes; Saucisse pili brochette
Regional or cuisine relevance: Burundi, Rwanda, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania.

Definition: Raw and lightly cooked accompaniments served alongside skewers and stews.
Inclusion rules: Kachumbari, acar, cabbage and onion salad, chilli and onion relish, salted tomato.
Exclusion rules: Salads composed as a course (FAM-03); cooked side vegetables.
Alternative names and synonyms: Kachumbari; Kachumber; Acar; Tomato onion relish; Shito (as a relish reference)
Regional or cuisine relevance: Rwanda, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania.

Definition: Cooked rice dishes served as a base or as a dish in their own right.
Inclusion rules: Pilau, biryani, kenchinji, rice and stew plates, rice with sauce.
Exclusion rules: Plain rice as a staple line (FAM-R01).
Alternative names and synonyms: Pilau; Biryani; Biriani; Kenchinji; Wali
Regional or cuisine relevance: Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya, Rwanda, Burundi.

Definition: Lake and river fish prepared grilled, fried or stewed.
Inclusion rules: Tilapia, mbadi, ndagala, isambaza, mukeke, samaki, catfish.
Exclusion rules: Imported shellfish dishes (FAM-11 general).
Alternative names and synonyms: Samaki; Mbadi; Ndagala; Mukeke; Isambaza; Isombe; Changu; Pike; Tilapia
Regional or cuisine relevance: Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda.

Definition: Fried, sweet and unleavened breads.
Inclusion rules: Chapati, mandazi, mahambri, vitumbua, mkate wa mchele, samosa.
Exclusion rules: Filled rolls and rolex (FAM-18); pastries (FAM-29).
Alternative names and synonyms: Chapati; Mandazi; Amandazi; Mahambri; Vitumbua; Mkate wa Mchele; Samosa; Samosas; Sughali
Regional or cuisine relevance: Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Burundi, Rwanda.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain; Bakery

Definition: Hot and cold cooked snacks sold informally or as a light meal.
Inclusion rules: Samosa, spring roll, egg roll, chips, chapati rolls, roasted maize, samosas with pili pili.
Exclusion rules: Starters served table-service (FAM-01).
Alternative names and synonyms: Samosa; Sughali; Spring roll; Egg roll; Chapati roll; Chips; Mahambri
Regional or cuisine relevance: Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain; Delivery-only kitchen

Definition: Rice-based principal dishes in the West African context.
Inclusion rules: Jollof rice, fried rice, waakye, rice and beans, palm nut rice.
Exclusion rules: Rice as a staple line only (FAM-R10).
Alternative names and synonyms: Jollof; Jollof rice; Waakye; Fried rice; Rice (breakfast); Rice with stew
Regional or cuisine relevance: Nigeria, Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Chain; Delivery-only kitchen

Definition: Stiff doughs eaten with soup or stew, sold by type and portion.
Inclusion rules: Fufu, banku, tuo zaafi, pounded yam, eba, semo, amala, omotuo, kankankan, konkonte.
Exclusion rules: Rice dishes (FAM-R09); porridge (FAM-02 boundary).
Alternative names and synonyms: Swallow; Fufu; Banku; Tuo zaafi; Tuo; Pounded yam; Poundo yam; Eba; Semo; Amala; Omutuo; Konkonte; Akpese
Regional or cuisine relevance: Ghana, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Liberia.

Definition: Soup and stew preparations served with a swallow or starch.
Inclusion rules: Light soup, okro soup, egusi soup, pepper soup, groundnut soup, palm nut soup, vegetable stew.
Exclusion rules: Stews served over rice (FAM-R09).
Alternative names and synonyms: Light soup; Okro soup; Egusi; Pepper soup; Groundnut soup; Palmnut soup; Gravy; Stew
Regional or cuisine relevance: Nigeria, Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia.

Definition: Fried pastry and batter snacks served as starters or snacks.
Inclusion rules: Samosa, puff-puff, spring roll, meat pie, doughnut, akara, moi moi.
Exclusion rules: Starters served table-service (FAM-01); full meals.
Alternative names and synonyms: Small chops; Chops; Puff-puff; Puff puff; Akara; Meat pie; Samosa; Samosas
Regional or cuisine relevance: Nigeria, Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain; Bar

Definition: Grilled meats and braai platters with pap and chakalaka.
Inclusion rules: Braai platter, wors, sosaties, snoek braai, boerewors rolls, fillet, lamb.
Exclusion rules: Grills in the general sense (FAM-08) where braai culture is not the context.
Alternative names and synonyms: Braai; Barbeque; BBQ; Wors; Sosaties; Boerewors; Snoek braai
Regional or cuisine relevance: South Africa, Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe.

Definition: Slow-cooked potjie dishes and Cape Malay curries.
Inclusion rules: Potjiekos, bobotie, denningvleis, bredie, Cape Malay curry.
Exclusion rules: Curries served with rice in other regions.
Alternative names and synonyms: Potjiekos; Bobotie; Denningvleis; Bredie; Cape Malay; Bobotie (Curries)
Regional or cuisine relevance: South Africa.

Definition: Small plates, biltong, koeksisters and street snacks.
Inclusion rules: Biltong, koeksister, samoosas, samosas, malva, bunny chow (see separate entry), sesame balls.
Exclusion rules: Desserts (FAM-26) where the item is sweet and plated as a dessert.
Alternative names and synonyms: Small plates; Biltong; Koeksister; Koeksisters; Samosas; Samosa; Malva; Milktart; Milk tart
Regional or cuisine relevance: South Africa, Namibia, Botswana.

Definition: Traditional leavened and unleavened breads and rolls.
Inclusion rules: Boerewors roll, bunny chow, koeksisters base, vetkoek, scones, bread rolls.
Exclusion rules: Burger buns (FAM-19); filled bunny chow (separate category entry).
Alternative names and synonyms: Bunny chow; Vetkoek; Boerewors roll; Koeksister; Scones; Bread rolls
Regional or cuisine relevance: South Africa, KwaZulu-Natal.

Definition: Cold and warm small plates served communally with flatbread.
Inclusion rules: Hummus, moutabal, baba ganoush, fattoush, labneh, brik, olives, pickles.
Exclusion rules: Hot starters (FAM-01) where the item is served hot as a course.
Alternative names and synonyms: Mezze; Meze; Mezedesh; Hummus; Moutabal; Baba ghanoush; Fattoush; Labneh; Tabel
Regional or cuisine relevance: Morocco, Tunisia, Algeria, Egypt, Libya.

Definition: Slow-cooked stews served with bread or couscous.
Inclusion rules: Tagine, tangia, couscous dishes, koshari, kabsa, masala stews.
Exclusion rules: Stews served with couscous as a named set (see FAM-R20).
Alternative names and synonyms: Tagine; Tangia; Tajine; Couscous; Koshari; Kabsa; Tajines; Ragout
Regional or cuisine relevance: Morocco, Tunisia, Algeria, Egypt, Libya.

Definition: Unleavened breads and savoury pastries served as a base or starter.
Inclusion rules: Khobz, msemen, bessara, baklava (sweet, FAM-26), samosa, briouate, pastilla.
Exclusion rules: Pizza; sweet pastries served as dessert.
Alternative names and synonyms: Khobz; Khobez; Msemen; Bessara; Briouate; Breek; Bricochs; Fatayer
Regional or cuisine relevance: Morocco, Tunisia, Algeria, Egypt.

Category / subcategory name: Combos and meal deals are items, not categories
Definition: Meal deals, mixed platters sold at a fixed price, and breakfast sets are composite sellable items built from other items.
Inclusion rules: Any item whose definition lists constituent items at a combined price.
Exclusion rules: Any category proposed to contain only composites; a business may display a 'Deals' surface, which is a named menu, not a category.
Alternative names and synonyms: Combo; Meal deal; Bundle; Set; Package; Platter; For two; Family meal
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Observed as choose-N platters, pastry selection boxes and brunch set compositions.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Category / subcategory name: Sides exist as both items and references
Definition: A side may be sold standalone as a menu line or referenced as a companion to another item.
Inclusion rules: Any item flagged as a side in at least one placement.
Exclusion rules: Any assumption that a side is always a modifier, or always a top-level category line.
Alternative names and synonyms: Side; Accompaniment; Extra; Add-on; Supplement; Garnish
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Breakfast, brunch, lunch, tea, dinner and late night are availability windows, never categories.
Inclusion rules: Any dimension value that describes when an item may be ordered.
Exclusion rules: Any category named for a time of day; use a named menu or a service-period filter instead.
Alternative names and synonyms: Meal occasion; Service period; Daypart; Served at
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain

Definition: Starter, main course and dessert as eating positions are a service convention assigned separately.
Inclusion rules: Any course assignment applied to an item or to a menu.
Exclusion rules: Any category named for a course position where the culinary category is available.
Alternative names and synonyms: Course; Course position; Sequence; First; Second; Main course position
Regional or cuisine relevance: Global. Formal French service may use many more courses than a casual menu.
Applicable business types: Independent restaurant; Hotel; Cafe; Bakery; Bar; Delivery-only kitchen; Chain
